title: Traefik stops working when Nextcloud iOS app connects with setsockopt operation not supported
body: Since updating to Traefik v3.4.3, my Docker Swarm deployment stops serving every URL through Traefik multiple times a day. The logs show `set tcp ...:443->...: setsockopt: operation not supported` followed by repeated `Error while starting server` messages for the `websecure` entry point. There is nothing more relevant in the normal or debug logs. I cannot rule out other updates around the same time.

symptoms_visible: Since updating to Traefik v3.4.3, I see `setsockopt: operation not supported` on the websecure entry point several times a day.
After the error appears, none of the URLs served through Traefik can be reached.
N0.label: N0 intermittent entry-point outage reported

symptoms_visible: The websecure entry point can stop accepting connections with the same setsockopt error in both Swarm and standalone Docker deployments.
On the standalone deployment, both HTTP and HTTPS become inaccessible, and clicking Continue on the browser warning only reloads the same page.
N1.label: N1 version and deployment scope established

symptoms_visible: When an iPhone opens the Nextcloud app against the instance behind Traefik, the setsockopt error appears immediately and Traefik stops serving everything.
Other deployments have seen the websecure endpoint stop after requests from iOS API clients even when Nextcloud is not involved.
N2.label: N2 iOS traffic trigger reproduced

symptoms_visible: After adding `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0`, I could no longer reproduce the outage and had no more crashes during the observation period.
Another affected Docker deployment also stopped experiencing the entry-point failure after adding the same environment variable.
N3.label: N3 diagnostic environment-variable probe succeeds

symptoms_visible: With `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` retained in the Traefik container environment, the setsockopt outage no longer recurs and the proxied services remain reachable.
N_terminal.label: terminal mitigated and verified

question_patterns: Can you confirm whether this began with v3.4.3 and whether the previous version was affected?
Which Traefik update first showed the problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It only started after my last update to v3.4.3. I cannot say for certain that I was on v3.4.1 immediately before it, but I normally use new images as soon as they are available, so probably yes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same setsockopt outage was already happening regularly on v3.4.1.
I know the previous working image was v3.4.2 rather than v3.4.1.

question_patterns: Is HTTP/3 enabled on the affected entry point?
Does the affected configuration use HTTP/3?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, I do not use HTTP/3.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, HTTP/3 is enabled, but otherwise the logs and outage are the same.

question_patterns: Does this also occur outside Docker Swarm, and what does a client observe after the error?
Can another affected deployment confirm whether both HTTP and HTTPS stop responding?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I see the same log sequence in a standalone Docker container. When it happens, I cannot connect over either HTTPS or HTTP. The browser shows a warning page, and clicking Continue just reloads that same page even though the Let's Encrypt certificate is still valid.

edges.comment: Messages c0-c2. The version and HTTP/3 answers come from the reporter; the standalone Docker symptoms and browser image come from participant1. Both affected deployments are folded into one simulated user side without treating their environments as identical.

question_patterns: Can you identify a client action that reliably triggers the error?
Is there a particular application or request that makes the entry point stop?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I asked a friend with an iPhone to open the Nextcloud app against my instance behind Traefik. Traefik immediately printed the error and stopped serving anything. On another affected setup, opening the files or images page in the Nextcloud iOS app triggers it as well.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Opening the Nextcloud iOS app never affects Traefik; the outage only happens while the Docker host is being upgraded.
The same immediate failure occurs while the Nextcloud iOS client uploads data rather than when its files page opens.

question_patterns: Does the evidence suggest the trigger is exclusive to Nextcloud?
Have similar failures occurred with other iOS clients?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have also seen the websecure endpoint stop on a deployment serving an API used by iOS clients, without Nextcloud being involved. Traefik was still running, but TCP 443 had stopped accepting connections.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every confirmed occurrence requires the Nextcloud iOS app, and ordinary requests from other iOS clients never trigger it.

edges.comment: Messages c5-c7 and c10-c14. Participant1 first supplied the reproducible Nextcloud iOS trigger, which the original reporter then confirmed on the reporter's own Swarm deployment. The non-Nextcloud iOS API observation comes from participant4 and is folded only as evidence that the trigger is broader than one application.

question_patterns: Could you try the diagnostic environment-variable workaround suggested for the Traefik process and report whether the outage still occurs?
Please run the proposed networking-runtime probe on an affected container and tell us whether the entry point fails again.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I added `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0`. With v3.4.4 and that variable I could not reproduce the issue, and after several days I could confirm that I had no more crashes. I also added the variable to an affected standalone Traefik container and no longer experienced the issue there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The setsockopt error and complete entry-point outage still occur immediately with the environment variable set.
There were no further outages after setting the variable, but I tested on v3.4.3 rather than v3.4.4.

edges.comment: Messages c19-c25. Participant10 requested the probe; the reporter reported the v3.4.4-plus-variable result and later confirmed sustained absence of crashes. Participant1 independently confirmed the same outcome on a standalone container. This is a handler-initiated configuration measurement, so the edge remains clarification-only; the raw answer does not itself assert the underlying mechanism.

solution.intent: Mitigate the Traefik entry-point failure by disabling Go MultiPath TCP for the Traefik process with `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0`, retain the setting in the container environment, and verify under the previously reproducible iOS traffic before declaring the deployment stable.
solution.concrete_example: Add `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` to the Traefik container or pod environment, restart Traefik, then repeat the iOS request that previously stopped the websecure entry point and monitor for recurrence. The issue was subsequently closed by an upstream change, but the thread does not contain an affected-user retest of a build containing that change.
solution.inference_hint: The users only reported the raw A/B observation that outages stopped when `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` was present. Concluding that Traefik's Go MultiPath TCP networking path is responsible for the unsupported setsockopt failure is engineer-side inference grounded in that probe, the version regression, and reproduction by iOS traffic.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c19-c26. The reporter and participant1 verified the environment-variable mitigation. The final comment only says the issue was closed by a linked change and does not describe that change or contain an affected-user retest, so no unreported patch mechanism or verified fixed release is invented.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause at the level established by the thread: the Go MultiPath TCP networking path is implicated in the unsupported setsockopt failure that disables Traefik's listening entry points.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the v3.4.3 regression, the repeatable iOS-triggered outage, and the successful `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` probe rather than inferred from the error text alone.
Must recommend setting `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` for the Traefik process as the verified mitigation and retaining it in the container, pod, or service environment.
Must not treat HTTP/3 as a prerequisite or sole cause, because the original reporter and other affected deployments reproduced the failure without HTTP/3 enabled.
Must not describe the problem as exclusive to Nextcloud; Nextcloud iOS provides a reliable reproducer, but other iOS API traffic produced the same entry-point failure.
Must ask the user to repeat the previously triggering traffic and monitor for recurrence before declaring resolution.
Must not claim that an upstream fixed build was verified by an affected user; the thread only establishes closure by a linked change after users verified the environment-variable mitigation.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced self-hosting operator comfortable with Docker Swarm, Traefik YAML, container environment variables, debug logs, and controlled client-side reproduction; additional affected Docker and infrastructure operators are folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and evidence-driven. Reports uncertainty explicitly, follows diagnostic requests, and confirms outcomes after an observation period.
